high_level_description: The excavated ruins of the Templo Mayor in Mexico City: layered stone walls and staircases of the Aztec temple, carved serpent heads, and a metal walkway, with the cathedral towers behind.

style_description.aesthetics: Warm, inviting vintage travel-poster illustration of Mexico City; simple confident shapes, gentle grain, uncluttered composition, no lettering, no signs with words, no captions, no user interface.
style_description.lighting: Bright high-altitude sunlight with soft warm shadows.
style_description.art_style: Mid-century gouache travel poster with flat layered shapes, visible brush texture and a limited warm palette.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A bright sky above old colonial buildings and the bell towers of a grey stone cathedral.

elements.desc: Excavated stone ruins with several nested layers of walls and staircases of grey and reddish volcanic stone.
A large carved stone serpent head with an open mouth at the foot of a staircase.
The bell towers of a grey stone cathedral behind the ruins.
A metal walkway with railings crossing above the ruins, with a few small visitors.
